searchText: <@194432762315407360> why are we closing https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/pull/9152 ? I find the arguments against it not strong enough and it makes sense. My understanding is that it is still up for discussion even if we dont want to include it for devnet-5 that doesnt meant the suggestion is to be disregarded it's kind of what I meant on the call as well, that I'd be back about this most people were OK with my proposal, but reth had an objection postponing to devnet-6 also gives us time to think about it im not sure there will be devnet-6 but would love to hear from <@&1070471163219824730> more I retracted my proposal on ACD because I don't want to hold up the devnet-5 process but also didn't fully understand the concern with 'authorization routing' is this mentioned somewhere? it was mentioned by Roman on the call like, they want the chainID in the object because it helps with some internal routing thing thanks for tagging. basically, the argument is that we are introducing a new primitive in the protocol and it provides 0 benefit to make it context dependent. authorizations can be generated and exchanged on their own, before they are ever bundled into one transaction. the closest analogy to this would be removing chain id from transaction object everywhere because the "blockchain" knows which chain id it has But when those tuples are exchanged, the chainId can be exchanged along side them, maybe, the block size cost saving is worth it? There are no savings on mainnet? byte vs u256 ? there is for sure savings these end up looking the same for `0x01` on mainnet ah, true. if we are talking strictly on mainnet. was thinking about all chains. imo this is strictly a client storage implementation detail. if you want, you can encode the transactions that way
